messages:
incident-bot: Pager: hosted-api(us-west1) queue length spike detected. p95 generation latency 2.1s -> 7.3s, p99 > 12s. GPU pool us-west-gpu-1 at 98% util, autoscaler failed to launch new nodes due to quota error. Escalating to oncall.

alice.oncall: saw the alert. digging into autoscaler logs now. any customer-facing reports?

megan.support: multiple customers reported increased timeouts and 429-ish errors around 11:04 PDT. support queue has 6 high-priority tickets (some Prod).

ben.sre: looking at metrics — queue length for hosted-gen queue jumped from ~120 -> ~4.6k in ~3m. request drop rate climbed from 0.2% -> 6.8%.

carol.prodops: what happened to autoscaler? `scale-controller` shows repeated API 403 from cloud quota endpoint. suspect quota or IAM token expired.

dave.runtime: confirming: runtime logs show continuous GC stalls not the cause. kernel output: `ERROR: unable to provision GPU instance: quotaExceeded` every attempt for the last 8 minutes.

alice.oncall: timeline — spike started 11:03:12, first autoscale attempt 11:04:01, repeated failures until 11:11:03. current backlog 4.1k requests. p95 6.9s p99 15.4s.

ben.sre: quick mitigation options: 1) enable fallback to smaller model variant to reduce GPU memory and run on existing nodes, 2) evict low-priority batch jobs and shift capacity, 3) temporary global rate-limit / shed non-authenticated traffic. Thoughts?

carol.prodops: eviction already in progress for batch jobs — kicking off eviction for pool-id us-west-batch-2. Initiating now.

megan.support: can we prioritize requests from paying customers? we have account IDs in head of queue.

alice.oncall: yes — create priority routing policy to promote requests with header X-Customer-Tier: premium. Doing a config flip on the router. Will post confirmation.

deploy-bot: Config change queued: promote-premium-route -> applying to gateway cluster (gw-2).

deploy-bot: Config applied on gw-2 at 11:12:10 PDT.

dave.runtime: starting fallback model rollout: v1-large -> v1-medium for hosted-gen-default. This reduces memory by ~30% and increases throughput. Rolling to 10% traffic now.

alice.oncall: after router flip + 10% fallback: queue dropped to ~2.8k within 4m. p95 down to 3.8s, p99 down to 9.1s. Good signal.

ben.sre: eviction freed 6 GPUs from batch pool, but autoscaler still returning quota errors for provisioning. We should request emergency quota increase as permanent fix, but that takes time.

carol.prodops: filing cloud quota request with CC to infra-leads and account team. Also opening short-lived reservation: attempt to allocate preemptible instances in us-west to warm up.

megan.support: notifying top affected customers with status update: short blurb that we are mitigating, some customers already seeing improved latency.

tim.sales: paste for customer comms: "We experienced a transient capacity event affecting hosted-gen in us-west. We have applied triage mitigations (priority routing, model fallback, eviction) and traffic is recovering. Further updates as we confirm full recovery."

alice.oncall: spinning up manual extra worker processes on existing nodes to accept more concurrent streams (increase threadpool from 64 -> 96) as a stopgap. Will monitor OOMs.

dave.runtime: note — increasing threadpool will raise memory pressure. I pushed config 11:16:02, node-level memory up ~9%. No OOMs observed yet.

ben.sre: queue down to ~1.1k after 20m of mitigation. p95 1.9s p99 4.5s. Still seeing a cohort of stuck requests that hit timeouts around 30s — investigating edge cases.

carol.prodops: quota request submitted ticket #CLOUD-98721, requested +12 GPUs for us-west. Filed as high priority.

megan.support: customers asked for ETA — can we give an estimate?

alice.oncall: ETA for full recovery depends on cloud quota approval or successful warm preemptibles. If quota approved in next hour we'll scale normally; otherwise plan is to keep fallback and priority routing for next 6 hours. Tell customers we expect continued improvement, but degrade gracefully for low-priority requests.

tim.sales: bumping to account execs and posting to top customers so they don't open more tickets.

dave.runtime: digging into why autoscaler hit quota — looks like a recent config change to provisioning account key rotation caused the 403 for certain instance types. Rolling back rotation for the autoscaler service account now.

alice.oncall: rollback applied at 11:27:45. Autoscaler attempting provisioning again.

deploy-bot: autoscaler-provision-job started provisioning attempts at 11:28:10.

ben.sre: first successful provisioning at 11:30:03 — 4 new GPU nodes. Pool util dropped to 82%. Queue down to 420. p95 1.1s p99 2.9s.

alice.oncall: marking service as recovering. Keeping incident open for postmortem and customer follow-ups.

carol.prodops: action items: 1) revert account key rotation process + add preflight check (owner: carol), 2) cloud quota review + baseline reservation (owner: ben), 3) improve autoscaler error visibility (owner: dave), 4) update runbook to enable priority routing (owner: alice).

megan.support: sending final mitigation update to affected customers now, will include thread link and timeline.

tim.sales: will join postmortem with customers that were impacted.

alice.oncall: finishing notes: root cause — autoscaler provisioning blocked by rotated/invalid service account key causing quota 403s; amplified by sudden traffic spike. Immediate mitigations: priority routing, model fallback, eviction of batch jobs, threadpool bump, manual provisioning. Recovery confirmed at 11:30 PDT.

incident-bot: Incident ack closed by alice.oncall at 11:31:00 PDT (severity reduced to SOC-LOW, follow-ups scheduled).

alice.oncall: creating incident doc in ops/incidents/hosted-us-west-2024-11-26 and assigning owners. Will ping for postmortem.

ben.sre: attaching brief metrics snapshot to the doc and a few logs. Will run a targeted test to reproduce autoscaler 403 with key rotation in staging.

carol.prodops: closing loop with cloud account team to request a quota baseline and pre-approved ephemeral bump for future spikes.

megan.support: thanks everyone — support will follow up customers with timeline and remediation steps.

alice.oncall: handing off to oncall secondary (ben.sre) for the night monitoring. I am off rotation in 10m.

ben.sre: taking handoff. I have dashboard alerts at 1/3 severity. If queue > 600 reopen page.

megan.support: leaving a note for CS: affected accounts list saved in incident doc.

alice.oncall: thanks team.
